judgedItems.admissionAndRed: **(a) Admission and RED discipline.** The B14-0A recommendation was followed: the helpers were registered in the admission commit, so RED is test-only and the helper is dead product code at RED (verified by grep). Product behaviour at RED is byte-identical to the baseline, so all 22 RED failures are genuine.
judgedItems.ordering: **(b) Ordering, per surface (read from the head).**
judgedItems.codes1008And1011: **(c) 1008/1011 and terminality.** refuseFogSocket('policy') = typed Close AUTH_REJECTED fog-projection-unavailable, then close(1008, reason); the client's Close handler sets closedByCaller and never reconnects. refuseFogSocket('unavailable') = typed Error INTERNAL_ERROR 'match configuration unavailable', then close(1011, reason); the client has no Close frame, so handleSocketClose schedules a reconnect (pinned by the real connect() row: reconnects 1 vs 0). Both frames interpolate only matchId, ts, fixed code and fixed reason. The B14-0A 1011/false semantics are preserved: false still means projection available, and the 14 seams pin async () => false, with the type pin in the owned suite. CF-S-2 is decided and pinned: an unreadable live config refuses every recipient (actor included) with Error+1011 instead of silently withholding; the frame was never numbered, so the actor's resume replays its own declaration and the opponent still does not receive it. One consistency nit is F2.
judgedItems.seamGuard: **(d) Seam guard (CF-B14B-1, folding CF-B14A-2).** The owned suite requires the byte-exact canonical block exactly once in each of the 14 allowlisted suites (split-count === 1), no other mention of the module in those files, the set of test files naming fogMatchAdmission equal to exactly 14 + matchHistoryFog + itself, no computed-path jest.mock/doMock/unstable_mockModule/setMock anywhere under src (first alternative catches identifiers, template literals and arrays; second catches a literal followed by + or .), no jest.spyOn on a capability export, no mention in jest.config.js / jest.setup.js / jest.setup.a11y.ts, and the live module unmocked (isMockFunction false, identity with jest.requireActual for all three exports). The matchHistoryFog tripwire is untouched (B14-0A control). Residual evasions are jest['mock'] / aliased jest.mock, a consumer-module mock, a moduleNameMapper regex that does not spell the module name, and tests outside src/ (my R4; the walk covers only src while Jest roots also include scripts and openspec). These are exotic; the unmocked-identity assertion is what makes the refusal proof itself robust, and it holds.
judgedItems.completeness: **(e) Completeness of WS private reads.** Live events (all broadcastEvent callers: publication, journal authority, lobby intents, command results, reconnect lifecycle, resumePendingEventPublications via onlyUndelivered) route through publishEvent; join/replay/rejoin/ack-isolation resume and the rewind-rebuilt replay route through sendReplay; the legacy P2P callback is handled; LobbyUpdated is gated behind a successful replay. Non-event broadcasts (MatchPaused/MatchResumed, closeMatch's Close) carry no battle state. Because admission refuses every fog-on socket, a fog-on match can no longer acquire an attached socket, so the live and replay refusals are defence in depth for pre-existing or test-attached sockets. Residual channels outside this manifest: the legacy channel broadcasts rejections to every channel listener (F5), lobby summaries (CF-B14A-8), /head (B14-HEAD), /timeline (CF-B14A-7).
orderingBullets: admitSocket (ServerMatchHost.ts:704-756): viewerResolver.resolve (durable seat membership) -> matchLacksRevealProjection -> refuse+detach+return null, else attachSocket. A stranger throws AuthorizedViewerError before the config read and gets the pre-existing Error+Close AUTH_REJECTED, now physically 1008; membership-infrastructure failure gets Close INTERNAL_ERROR + 1011. The fog branch is unreachable before membership. One store read for a stranger versus two for a member is not a disclosure (the stranger's bytes are unchanged from Main).

publishEvent (ServerMatchHostEvents.ts:266-322): meta is read first (it always was, for the sealed-choice audience context), membership is resolved per player, and the refusal fires only for recipients with a resolved viewer; a viewer-less (non-member) attached socket still continue's silently as before, so the fog reason never reaches it. The refusal precedes frame shaping, the fog filter, guardLiveEvent, the onlyUndelivered check, admit() and assign(), so a refused frame consumes no delivery number (my R3 confirms this is pinned). fogMeta now tolerates meta.config undefined (author's crash mutant). The seat arguments and seat-before-GM order inside the fog-filter branch are unchanged bytes.

sendReplay (ServerMatchHostReplay.ts:80-139): resolveJoinViewer (membership) -> refusal -> getReplayEventsForPlayer/getEventsFromSeq -> stream. The event read moved below the refusal (pinned by the getEvents spy row: 0 reads for join/replay/legacy). handleSessionJoin resolves the viewer first and passes it as admittedViewer, so no double resolution; LobbyUpdated is only sent after sendReplay returned true. The host wrappers detach on false for both sendReplay and handleSessionJoin.

handleReconnectRequest (ServerMatchHostReplay.ts:243-290): legacy peer metadata decides member; only a metadata member triggers the config read; 'policy' then re-verifies the durable current seat through a fresh AuthorizedViewerResolver(MatchSeatMembershipSource) and answers FOG_REFUSAL only when current, else the pre-existing generic 'Match in progress'; 'unavailable' answers the generic reason. A non-member falls through to answerReconnectRequest, whose own first check rejects with 'Match in progress' before any event read; the host peer who used to be 'ignored-host' now gets the reject (member, not a leak). Fog-off is the unchanged call.
No raw fallback anywhere: every refusal returns before the stream, and the no-playerId raw sendReplay hook also refuses under fog-on (F4 below).

Known-off / flag-omitted: matchLacksRevealProjection returns false for {fogOfWar:false} and for {} (pinned), the fog-off GM co-op row and the seats-undefined row pass at RED and GREEN, and the 14 seamed suites plus the regression set pass.

items.finding: Membership-before-policy is pinned only at admitSocket ('gives a non-member generic auth'). The publication-guard failure path changed from an Error frame carrying the guard message (socket left open and attached) to a Close INTERNAL_ERROR 'viewer projection unavailable' + close(1011) + detach. The redaction is good (the guard messages are the fixed notAViewer/projectionFailed strings anyway) and the closePolicy allows 1011 terminal refusals, but it is a behaviour change the PR body describes only as "join refusals now close physically", and it makes 1011 terminal here while the same code is non-terminal in refuseFogSocket('unavailable'). My R2 (revert to the old Error frame) survives 28/28: nothing pins it. Either pin it with one row (guardReplayFrames failure -> exactly one Close, close 1011, detached) and name the Error->Close change in the PR body, or keep the old Error kind and only add the physical close.

The positive legacy case is unpinned: 'rejects the legacy reconnect callback before replay' asserts only toHaveBeenCalled(). My R1 (current-seat check always false, so a current member also gets 'Match in progress') survives 28/28. Fail-safe direction, but the PR body's "a metadata peer gets the fog reason only after the durable seat confirms current membership" is half-pinned (the negative half is W07). Pre-existing channel design (the same channel carries replay streams in the shared Y doc), P2P fallback only; no action for B14-0.

lifecycle.detach(socket) in admitSocket's fog branch is a no-op: the socket is only attached after this point. My R5 removes it and survives 28/28 (equivalent). Harmless; a comment or removal avoids implying the socket was attached.

The rewind-rebuilt replay calls the module-level handleSessionJoin, so a refused socket on that path is physically closed by refuseFogSocket but not lifecycle-detached until the transport close callback runs cleanup (or the heartbeat reaps it). Fog-on sockets cannot be attached after this PR, so it is unreachable in production; U26 (rewind owner) may want to route the rebuilt replay through the host wrapper that detaches.
The seam-guard walk covers src only; Jest roots also include scripts and openspec. My R4 (a seam-bearing suite under scripts/__tests__) passes the guard. Extend walk(...) to the three Jest roots.

'fog-off projection metadata absent does not become a policy refusal' asserts only the absence of the fog reason; a membership failure on seats-undefined would still pass it. Add expect(admitSocket).not.toBeNull() and a ReplayEnd assertion so the acceptance clause "otherwise-authorized reads remain functional" is pinned.

authority.verdict: PASS (membership precedes policy on all four surfaces; no privilege is a fog exemption)
authority.reviewer: **Authority.** Membership precedes policy on all four surfaces (admitSocket, publishEvent per recipient, sendReplay/handleSessionJoin, legacy callback with durable re-verification). Host, GM-without-seat, spectator and same-side players receive the same refusal: no privilege is a fog exemption. Non-members' bytes are unchanged from Main apart from the physical close code. The server stays authoritative: clients cannot influence the decision (it reads only the store).

replay.verdict: PASS (refused frames are never numbered; resume stays gapless; no journal or reducer change)
replay.reviewer: **Replay.** No event, journal, reducer or cursor-persistence change. Refused frames are never numbered (R3), so a reconnecting viewer's delivery sequence stays gapless and the from-cursor resume still owes the withheld frame (pinned for the actor's own declaration). stampReplayDeliveries is unchanged. Rewind ceiling handling is untouched.

idempotency.reviewer: **Idempotency.** Every refusal is read-only: no delivery assigned, no ack, no epoch, no audit or outbox write, no match row update. refuseFogSocket swallows send/close errors and detach is idempotent, so a second publish against an already-refused socket is a no-op (pinned: send called once across two broadcasts).

concurrency.reviewer: **Concurrency.** attachedSockets() is a snapshot, so detaching during the fan-out loop is safe. Config is immutable after creation (no update route), so the two reads in a fog-on admission or the config-then-seat reads in the legacy path cannot straddle a toggle; a seat revocation between them only tightens. Two concurrent publishEvents against the same fog-on socket both refuse; ws ignores close() on a CLOSING socket and the second send throws into the catch.
